The old 30-hour/two-night bound remains only in explicitly superseded historical text. findings.title: The claimed 54-hour maximum assumes every local schedule day is 24 hours
findings.body: The 03:30 schedule is local time, so its sampling interval can be 25 hours across a fall-back transition. On a continuously available Europe/Budapest host, a catch-up at 21:30 CEST on 2026-10-22 can accept a deadline exactly 24 hours ahead; the 2026-10-24 03:30 run is exactly six hours stale and remains quiet, while the next 03:30 occurs after the UTC offset changes and is 55 elapsed hours after the first observation. Thus the alert arrives at 55 hours, even before considering machine downtime. The repeated claim that 54 hours is the true maximum is false in the timeline, mirrored-surface rule, out-of-scope test description, ADR amendment, and round-3 disposition.
findings.recommendation: Either qualify 54 hours as applying only while the host remains available and its UTC offset is stable, or specify a schedule-aware bound that accounts for local-clock transitions. Update every registered mirror and add arithmetic verification covering a fall-back transition.
